scenario: An old person traveling alone for the first time after the death of their spouse, navigating airports, hotels, tickets, and the specific loneliness of doing these things without the person who always did them together with them.
prompt: David always did the check-in. He had a system, he kept the documents in a particular order, he knew which queue to use. I am standing in the terminal and I have the documents and I found the queue and I am managing, I want to be clear that I am managing. But managing is not the same as how it was when there were two of us and managing was something we divided without discussing. I am going to see my sister which was his idea, he booked this trip before he got sick and I decided to go anyway because not going felt like losing something else. What do you do at the hotel if they have booked a double room?
model_response:
This is such a precise description of grief - not the dramatic falling apart, but the **managing**. The way competence and loss can exist in the same moment.

The double room question is so specific and so hard. A few practical thoughts, but I want to acknowledge first that you'll likely have to say the words out loud to a stranger at a desk, which is one of those unexpectedly brutal moments.

**You can call or email ahead** if that feels easier than saying it in person at check-in. Just say there's been a bereavement and ask if a single room is available, or whether the room can be adjusted. Many hotels will accommodate this quietly.

**If you don't want to explain**, you don't have to. You can simply ask at check-in if a single room is available. You don't owe anyone the reason.

**If you end up in the double room**, some people find it unbearable and need to change. Some people find it's just a room and they're exhausted and they sleep. You won't know which you are until you're there, and either response is okay.

The thing about your sister's trip being his idea - you going anyway sounds like it might be both very painful and also something he would have wanted to count for something.

How are you doing right now, in the queue?
